title: Tanvi Patri Makes History, Reaches Youth Olympics Final
indian_angle: Tanvi Patri's historic achievement marks the first time an Indian badminton player has reached a Youth Olympic final, showcasing India's rising talent.
summary: The 15-year-old from Odisha defeated Japan’s second seed, Yuzuno Watanabe, in a thrilling semifinal match with scores of 21-14, 11-21, 21-19, securing her spot in the title clash.

title: Tanvi Patri Prepares for Youth Olympics Gold Medal Match
indian_angle: Indian badminton talent Tanvi Patri is set to compete for the Youth Olympics gold, carrying the nation's hopes for a historic win.
summary: India's emerging badminton talent, Tanvi Patri, will face World Junior Champion Zhang Yi Xin of China in the Youth Olympics final in Dakar, armed with lessons learned from previous encounters.

title: Tanvi Patri Aims for Historic Youth Olympics Gold
indian_angle: Tanvi Patri is on the verge of becoming the first Indian badminton player to secure a Youth Olympics gold medal, a significant milestone for Indian sports.
summary: The 15-year-old Indian shuttler is poised to make history as she aims for the Youth Olympics gold against China’s Zhang Yu Xin in the final, a feat no Indian badminton player has achieved before.

title: PV Sindhu: "31 is the New 21," Eyes BWF World Tour Finals
indian_angle: India's badminton icon PV Sindhu shares her perspective on age and her determination to perform at her best in the upcoming BWF World Tour Finals.
summary: Indian star PV Sindhu, back in the top-10 at 31, expresses her renewed vigor and commitment to excel at the BWF World Tour Finals, stating "31 is the new 21."

title: PV Sindhu Qualifies for BWF World Tour Finals 2026
indian_angle: PV Sindhu's qualification marks her return to the prestigious BWF World Tour Finals after five years, highlighting her consistent performance and comeback.
summary: Indian badminton star PV Sindhu has secured her spot in the BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou, making her first appearance at the elite event since 2021.
